control_name: JIT Compiler Hardening (JIT Restriction / V8 Sandbox)
description: Restricts or hardens Just-In-Time compilation in language runtimes and browser engines to prevent type confusion exploitation. Encompasses three postures: (1) JIT disabling — turning off JIT compilation entirely via flags (--jitless in V8, javascript.options.ion in Firefox) which eliminates JIT-spraying and JIT-based type confusion at the cost of performance; (2) V8 Sandbox enforcement — a hardware-backed memory cage that isolates JIT-compiled code and V8 heap objects from the rest of the process address space, requiring an additional sandbox escape even after achieving type confusion; (3) JIT tiering restrictions — limiting optimization tiers to reduce the surface of speculative type assumptions that can be violated. Applicable to Chromium-based browsers, Node.js, Electron applications, and SpiderMonkey-based runtimes. Complements CME-113 (CFI/Shadow Call Stack) which prevents type-confused pointers from redirecting control flow in native code.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: JIT disabling eliminates the type speculation attack surface entirely; V8 Sandbox requires the attacker to chain a sandbox escape after the type confusion, converting a single-step exploit into a multi-step chain that must defeat both the type system and the memory cage
V8 Sandbox confines the impact of type confusion to the sandbox boundary; the attacker cannot directly reach renderer process memory or OS resources without an additional escape primitive
conditions: Requires V8 Sandbox posture specifically — JIT disabling (posture 1) eliminates exploitation entirely making scope moot, but JIT tiering restrictions alone (posture 3) do not add a scope boundary

verification.method: Verify JIT hardening is enabled in browser or runtime configuration. Check for jitless mode, V8 Sandbox flags, or JIT disabling in Firefox preferences.

commands.expected: Non-empty output — --jitless flag found in Chromium launch configuration
Non-empty output — javascript.options.ion preference found (should be set to false)
Non-empty output — V8 sandbox flags available in the Node.js runtime

commands.command: reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge" /v JITDisabled 2>nul & reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome" /v JITDisabled 2>nul

remediation.name: Chromium/Chrome JIT disabling via managed policy

steps.description: Create a managed policy directory for Chromium-based browsers if it does not exist
Write a managed policy that passes --jitless to V8, disabling JIT compilation entirely (eliminates JIT spraying and type confusion attack surface at the cost of JavaScript performance)

remediation.name: Firefox JIT disabling via autoconfig preferences

steps.description: Enable Firefox autoconfig by creating the autoconfig loader in the defaults/pref directory
Write autoconfig file that disables IonMonkey JIT, Baseline JIT, and WebAssembly JIT (eliminates JIT-based type confusion and JIT spraying at the cost of JavaScript performance)

remediation.name: Chrome/Edge JIT disabling via Group Policy registry

steps.description: Disable JIT in Google Chrome via Group Policy registry key (applies to all users on the machine)
Disable JIT in Microsoft Edge via Group Policy registry key

remediation.verify: reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome" /v JITDisabled & reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge" /v JITDisabled
